chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There was a group of people in the presence of my father, and they differed regarding Al-Nabeez. Some of them said, 'The cup which intoxicates is prohibited.' And some of them said, 'A little of what intoxicates, and its lot is prohibited.' So they referred the matter to my father (peace be upon him). So my father said: 'Do you see the measure (qist)? If not for what is poured into it first, it would be full. And similarly, the other cup, if not for the first one, it would not intoxicate.'

He (the narrator) said, 'Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever enters one vein from his veins with a little of what a lot of it would intoxicate, Allah will punish that vein with three hundred and sixty types from the types of punishment.'.

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Al-Nabeez (a specific type of fermented drink)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Al-Nabeez and the principle of intoxication in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia juristic principle of 'Kathiruhu Yuskiru Qaliluhu' (the intoxicating quantity determines the ruling for the small quantity) through Imam al-Sadiq’s analogy of a measuring vessel, clarifying that the presence of the intoxicant itself, rather than its volume, dictates prohibition. It reinforces the severity of minor consumption by citing a Prophetic tradition warning of specific divine punishments for the veins carrying the intoxicant, a concept central to Shia fiqh regarding khamr. This discussion highlights the methodological rigor in distinguishing between the substance's nature and its measurable effects.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There was a group of people in the presence of myasws fatherasws. So they had differed regarding Al-Nabeez, so some of them said, ‘The cup which intoxicates, it is Prohibited’, and some of them said, ‘A lot of which intoxicates, a little of it is Prohibited’. So they referred the matter to myasws fatherasws. So Myasws fatherasws said: ‘Your views are equitable. If only you had not placed in it what filled it, and similar to that is the other cup, if only it the first one was what intoxicates’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who enters into one vein from his veins, a little of what a lot of it would intoxicate, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Punish that vein with three hundred and sixty types from the types of the Punishment’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Once there was a group of people with my father and they had different views about al-Nabidh. Certain ones among them said, “The cupful (of al-Nabidh) which is intoxicating is unlawful.” Others said, “Al-Nabidh in small quantity does not intoxicate but it is unlawful in large quantity.” They referred the matter to my father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who said, “On the basis of fairness and justice if nothing has been placed in the cup it would never become full. This applies to the other cup also. If nothing has been placed in, it would not intoxicate.”

He (the Imam) said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘If a small quantity of that which in large quantity intoxicates, enters one’s vein, Allah will make that vein suffer because of three hundred sixty kinds of torments.”””
